title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Throughout, k is the base ring, L_* is the simplicial k-module n ↦ k^{[n]} of functions on the vertices of Δ^n, and Ψ_* is its augmentation kernel (inferred from the previous page). The page sets up four related objects, each a cosimplicial simplicial k-module or its partial normalizations.

(1) The cochain object. ℂ^*_* is (m,n) ↦ ℂ^{[m]}_{[n]} = k^{Hom_Δ(Δ^m,Δ^n)}. For fixed n, m ↦ k^{Hom_Δ(Δ^m,Δ^n)} is the cosimplicial module of all cochains on Δ^n. For fixed m, ℂ^{[m]}_* is a simplicial module that represents m-cochains: by Yoneda, Hom_{sSet}(X_*, ℂ^{[i]}_*) ≅ k^{X_{[i]}} = Hom_ens(X_{[i]}, k).

(2) The normalized cochain object. C^·_* = Λ^{·+1} L_*. Then C^m_{[n]} = Λ^{m+1} k^{[n]} ≅ k^{Inj_Δ(Δ^m,Δ^n)}, with basis e_{i0}∧…∧e_{im} for i0<…<im. These are the normalized (non-degenerate) m-cochains of Δ^n: 0 if m>n, and k if m=n.
- The simplicial structure in n matches the cochain one. For increasing f, Λ^{m+1}f^* sends a basis cochain to the cochain c with c(σ) = coefficient on f∘σ when f∘σ is injective, and 0 otherwise.
- Consequently Hom(X_*, Λ^{i+1}L_*) ≅ ℂ^i(X_*), the non-degenerate cochains. This is a direct summand of k^{X_{[i]}}, the complement of the degenerate part (‘fact. dir.’).

(3) Normalizing in the simplicial direction. Hom^!(Δ^m,Δ^n) is the set of increasing maps whose image contains [0,n−1]. The function module on it is exactly the Moore normalization ∩_{i<n} ker d_i of n ↦ k^{Hom(Δ^m,Δ^n)}, since ker d_i consists of functions vanishing on maps missing i.
- For Λ^{m+1}L the injective maps with image ⊇ [0,n−1] exist only for n=m and n=m+1, one each.
- So under Dold–Kan, Λ^{m+1}L_* corresponds to the two-term complex k (deg m) → k (deg m+1). This agrees with rank binom(n+1,m+1) = binom(n,m) + binom(n,m+1).
- The doubly normalized bicomplex ℂ^·_· therefore has k in bidegrees (m,m) and (m,m+1). The unnormalized term at n=m+1 is Λ^{m+1}k^{m+2} = k^{m+2}, and the connecting map is ‘diagonal’. This is the bookkeeping behind the contractibility of the cochains of Δ^n onto k.

(4) Chains and duality. Chains are ℂ_*(X) = k^{(X_*)}, with cochains ℂ^*(X) = ℂ_*(X)^∨ and normalized ℂ^·(X) = ℂ_·(X)^∨. The normalized chains are a direct factor (ND, the non-degenerate part) of all chains. Dual objects ℂ_*^* = (ℂ^*_*)^∨ etc. are listed.

Purpose: this is preparation for the next page, which recovers X_* from the functor F_X = Hom(X_*, −) on simplicial modules. There one gets Hom(F_X, F_{Δ^n}) ≅ Hom(ℂ^·(X), ℂ^·(Δ^n)) ≅ k[X_n]^{∨∨}. In the context of the cote, the goal is to compare cochains on simplices, written as Λ^{•+1}L, with the divided-power de Rham complex Γ(L)⊗Λ(Ψ) of the algebraic simplices, as on the previous page. That comparison is a PD, integral analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(•,*) and the Whitney/integration map.
errors: The marginal annotations comparing ℂ^{[m]}_n (all maps) and C^{[m]}_n (injective maps) — ‘iso si n ≠ m+1’, ‘iso si m ≥ n’ — are partly crossed out and inconsistent as written. For example, at n=m+1 the only map with image ⊇ [0,m] is the identity-type injection, so the two normalized pieces agree there.
The entry ‘C^{[m]}_{m+1} = Λ^{m+1}k^{m+2} = k^{m+2}’ gives the unnormalized term. Its normalized part is k, which is the only consistent reading of ‘k si n=m+1’.

ideas.what: The simplicial module n ↦ k^{Hom(Δ^i,Δ^n)} represents i-cochains: Hom(X_*, ℂ^{[i]}_*) ≅ k^{X_i}
ideas.modern_name: Representability of cochains by cochains on standard simplices (Yoneda; Eilenberg–MacLane/Kan; Sullivan's A(X) = Hom(X, ∇(•,*)))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan, Eilenberg–MacLane; Sullivan (1977) and Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for the forms version

ideas.what: Normalized cochains of Δ^n identified, as a simplicial module in n, with the exterior powers Λ^{m+1}(k^{[n]}); hence Hom(X, Λ^{i+1}L) = non-degenerate i-cochains
ideas.modern_name: Exterior-power description of normalized cochains of standard simplices; closely related to Whitney elementary forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Whitney (1957) for the forms analogue

ideas.what: Under Dold–Kan, Λ^{m+1}L_* is the two-term complex k → k in degrees m, m+1, via the Moore normalization by Hom^! (maps whose image contains [0,n−1])
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan normalization of exterior powers of the simplicial module of vertex-functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Kan; exterior powers of simplicial modules studied by Dold–Puppe (1961)

ideas.what: Duality between chain and cochain bicomplexes, and normalized chains as a direct factor of all chains
ideas.modern_name: Normalized vs unnormalized (co)chains; Eilenberg–MacLane normalization theorem

missed.claim: Writing cochains on Δ^n as Λ^{•+1}(L) with L = k^{[n]}, and setting this against the PD de Rham complex Γ(L)⊗Λ(Ψ) of the algebraic simplex via Koszul-type maps (previous page), puts the cochain/de Rham comparison into Koszul-complex form. It is the same mechanism by which Whitney forms appear as images of the Koszul operator in finite element exterior calculus (Arnold–Falk–Winther). There it is done over ℝ, whereas here it is done over an arbitrary k with divided powers.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic commutative cochain models (PD forms on simplices, binomial-ring models of Toën, Horel, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov) need an explicit integral Whitney-type comparison map. This page shows Grothendieck setting up exactly that bookkeeping around 1976, though only at the level of routine identifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of careful but essentially standard bookkeeping: representability of cochains, normalized cochains as exterior powers, and Dold–Kan normalization. It matters mainly as context for Grothendieck's 1976 project of a divided-power de Rham model for simplicial cochains, which is itself not well documented. The page contains no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the condition defining Hom^!(Δ^m,Δ^n) is that the image contains [0,n−1] (i.e. ‘l'image contient [0,n−1]’). This matches the Moore normalization ∩_{i<n} ker d_i.
‘pm_*(k)’ is unclear in the image; probably a notation for the simplicial module m ↦ k^{Hom_Δ(Δ^m,Δ^n)}, with indices garbled.
‘C^{[m]}_{[n]} = Λ^{m+1}k^{Δ^n} = k^{Inj_Δ(Δ^m,Δ^n)}’ — the exponent reads ‘Inj_Δ’, consistent with the mathematics.
‘fact. dir. com’ should read as ‘facteur direct’ (perhaps ‘facteur direct canonique’).
